name: The Old St Lucie Cherry of the Fuveszkert

location.address: ELTE Fuveszkert (botanical garden), roughly 80 metres along the main path from the entrance at Illes utca 25, Jozsefvaros

access: Paid entry, ELTE Fuveszkert botanical garden. Adult ticket 2200 Ft (2026 pricing), open daily 9:00-17:00 in main season (ticket office closes 16:30); hours vary by season, check before visiting
transport: M3 metro to Nagyvarad ter, then roughly 5-10 minute walk through Orczy-kert to the garden entrance on Illes utca
verify_notes: Species is Prunus mahaleb, Hungarian 'sajmeggy' (St Lucie cherry), normally a short-lived shrub or small tree to 6m; this specimen is 11.2m tall, 339cm trunk circumference, 12m crown diameter, unusually large and old for the species, which is itself the surprising fact to lead with. It PREDATES the botanical garden: it stood on the private estate of Marton Szeleczky (an imperial loyalist/royalist noble) before the property passed to the Festetics family in 1798, and the University bought the c.10-hectare Festetics castle garden in 1847 (with support from Palatine Archduke Joseph, per pestbuda) to found today's ELTE Fuveszkert, Hungary's oldest botanical garden (founded 1771 at an earlier Nagyszombat site, moved here 1847). So this tree witnessed a private noble estate become a public botanical garden. It is a solitary specimen next to the main path, described as easily reached on foot, wheelchair or with a stroller (per termeszetjaro.hu). Both sources agree on species, ~250-year age and the Szeleczky/Festetics/1847 history without disagreement; pestbuda.hu is the Hungarian Values Register (Magyar Ertektar) announcement, termeszetjaro.hu is a dedicated nature-site profile with the measurements. A third source (jozsefvaros.hu, headline 'may still have 500 good years left') was found via search but the URL redirect-looped and could not be fetched within the timeout; not used as one of the two sources, listed here for a future pass. Coordinates are the garden's centroid (geocoded via Nominatim), not a surveyed point for the tree itself, since no source gives GPS; the tree is roughly 80m along the main axis from the entrance per termeszetjaro.hu, which is more precise than the pin conveys, worth tightening on a future pass with a site plan or photo geolocation.

best_time.label: April into May, when the sajmeggy flowers white and fragrant

name: The Count's Mulberry of Karolyi Garden

location.address: Karolyi kert (Karolyi Garden), beside the perimeter wall near the Ferenczy Istvan utca entrance gate, Belvaros, Budapest V. kerulet

access: Free, open access, Karolyi kert (public park in central Budapest), opens 8:00 daily, closes at sunset (seasonal)
transport: Ferenciek tere metro (M3), roughly 7 minute walk; also close to Astoria (M2) and Kalvin ter (M3/M4)
verify_notes: Likely the oldest white mulberry in Hungary, possibly planted in the late 1700s during Count Antal Karolyi's baroque redesign of the garden after he bought the adjoining palace in 1768, or possibly during a later 1830s modernisation under Gyorgy Karolyi; exact planting date and planter unknown, both sources say so plainly rather than guessing a date. Trunk is famously thick: pestbuda.hu says it takes two adults with arms spread to encircle the furrowed trunk. History both sources agree on: it stood through Palatine Joseph's 1795 inaugural reception at the palace and Alexandra Pavlovna's 1800 name-day ball (both thrown in the garden), the great Pest flood of 1838 when the palace sheltered hundreds of refugee families, and the 1848-49 revolution's aftermath, when General Haynau made the palace his headquarters and Batthyany's arrest is associated with the same period. Currently in relatively good health but has been heavily pruned for safety/health reasons per pestbuda. FOKERT (Budapest's official parks authority) also has a dedicated 'Nevezetes fak' (notable trees) registry page for this exact tree (https://fokert.budapestikozmuvek.hu/eperfa-a-karolyi-kertben-v-keruletnevezetes-fak, same source type used for bud_002's pagoda tree) but the page is JS-rendered and returned no extractable text this pass; worth a proper fetch on a future pass, not counted as one of the two sources here. Stands beside the garden's perimeter wall near the Ferenczy Istvan utca gate; exact tree-level coordinates not found, pin is the garden's Ferenczy utca edge. This tree pairs naturally with bud_003 (Erzsebet ter Black Locust), roughly 1.3km away in the same central Belvaros district, and could anchor or extend a downtown walk alongside it.

best_time.label: June into July, when the mulberries ripen

name: The Old Acacia of Szechenyi Square
age_estimate: documented as 227 years (planted 1789), though disputed; possibly considerably younger

location.address: Szechenyi Istvan ter, on the traffic island near the Buda-side approach to the Chain Bridge, Budapest V. kerulet

access: Free, open access, but stands on a traffic island on Szechenyi Istvan ter surrounded by roads; reached on foot via pedestrian crossings only, not a park setting
transport: Close to Deak Ferenc ter and the Buda-side approach to the Chain Bridge; several city bus and tram routes serve Szechenyi Istvan ter directly
verify_notes: GENUINE AGE DISPUTE, deliver both figures per the rules, do not pick a winner. Az Ev Faja (Tree of the Year, submitted by the Belvarosi Szabadegyetem) and most popular coverage give 227 years old as of 2015/2016 (planted 1789, 'contemporary with the French Revolution', older than the Chain Bridge, the Academy of Sciences building and the Gresham Palace, the last survivor of a Danube-side avenue planted in the 1780s). BUT pestbuda.hu's own historian Viczian Zsofia directly disputes this in the same source, using photographic evidence: pre-1867 photos and postcards of the square show no tree at this spot, only a coronation mound of earth; an 1875 Gyorgy Klosz photo shows cart drivers standing where the tree supposedly already stood; the tree only appears as a substantial specimen in a 1930s postcard, which would put its real age closer to 120-150 years rather than 227. Both figures are given in age_min/age_max here; the writer should present this as an open dispute, not resolve it. Independent of age, both sources agree: black locust, severely leaning trunk (~4m circumference per evfaja.hu, height only ~6m due to the lean), propped by Fokert on wooden supports on iron beams since the 1980s with cushioned contact points, upper branch died in the 1980s removing its counterbalance, survived WWII bombing and the square's nine renamings. GPS coordinates (N 47 30.005' E 19 02.826') are given directly by evfaja.hu for this specific tree, converted here to decimal, hence location_precision confirmed rather than approximate; it stands on a paved traffic island, not inside a park, so the 'access' note is important for a visitor's expectations. ALIVE-NOW CAVEAT: both sources date to 2015-2016; searched for 2024-2025 Hungarian news of removal or collapse and found none, but no recent confirmation of survival either, so deliver flagged rather than confident. A 2016 pestbuda mention of 'planned redevelopment of Szechenyi ter' in coming years was not found to have removed the tree in any subsequent source.
